metric_identity.metric_name: Open-Source vs. Closed Model Market Share — Distribution of AI model usage, revenue, and enterprise adoption between open-source and proprietary/closed-source foundation models
metric_identity.source_report: Multiple sources: (1) OpenRouter / a16z 'State of AI: An Empirical 100 Trillion Token Study' (2025); (2) Menlo Ventures '2025 Mid-Year LLM Market Update' and '2025 State of Generative AI in the Enterprise'; (3) Stanford HAI AI Index Report 2025; (4) MIT Sloan analysis of open vs. closed models
metric_identity.publication_date: December 2025 (OpenRouter/a16z), July 2025 (Menlo Ventures mid-year), December 2025 (Menlo Ventures year-end), April 2025 (Stanford HAI)
metric_identity.methodology_notes: OpenRouter/a16z study: empirical analysis of over 100 trillion tokens routed through OpenRouter (5M+ developers, 300+ models, 60+ providers) from January to November 2025, measuring actual token consumption and revenue by model type. Menlo Ventures: survey and spend analysis of enterprise LLM procurement across major providers, tracking API spend and model selection. Stanford HAI: tracks newly released foundation models classified as open-source vs. proprietary, plus benchmark performance gaps. Hugging Face repository statistics track model uploads and downloads as a proxy for open-source ecosystem health.

metric_value.value: Key metrics: (1) Token usage share (OpenRouter, late 2025): open-source ~43%, closed-source ~42%, rest mixed/unclassified — a dramatic shift from May 2025 when closed models held ~70% of tokens; (2) Revenue share: closed models capture ~96% of revenue passing through OpenRouter despite only ~57-58% of token volume earlier in the study period; (3) Enterprise LLM market (Menlo Ventures mid-2025): Anthropic 32%, OpenAI 25%, Google 20%, Meta Llama 9%, other open-source ~14%; (4) Enterprise LLM spend year-end 2025: Anthropic 40%, OpenAI 27%; (5) Cost differential: closed models average $1.86/M tokens vs. open-source $0.23/M tokens (87% more expensive); (6) Model count: open-source represents 62.8% of all models by count, 65.7% of newly released foundation models in 2023 were open-source (up from 33.3% in 2021); (7) Hugging Face repository: 2M+ models accumulated by late 2025, second million reached in just 335 days vs. 1,000+ days for the first million; (8) Performance gap: open-source models reduced benchmark performance difference from 8% to 1.7% vs. closed models in a single year; (9) Enterprise AI investment: $37B total in 2025, tripling from prior year; enterprise LLM spend reached $8.4B by mid-2025
metric_value.unit: Percentage (market share), USD per million tokens (cost), count (models), USD billions (spending)
metric_value.geographic_scope: Global, with particular emphasis on US enterprise market for Menlo Ventures data and global developer community for OpenRouter data
metric_value.time_period: 2025 (January-November for OpenRouter; H1 and full-year for Menlo Ventures), with historical trend data from 2021-2024
metric_value.comparison_baseline: May 2025: closed models held ~70% of token share vs. ~43% by November 2025; Enterprise LLM share: OpenAI held 50% in late 2023, dropped to 25-27% by 2025; Open-source model releases: 33.3% of new foundation models in 2021 vs. 65.7% in 2023; Hugging Face: first 1M models took 1,000+ days, second 1M took 335 days; Performance gap: 8% benchmark difference in early 2024 narrowed to 1.7% by early 2025
metric_value.market_layer: model (primary — foundation model layer competition between open and closed providers), with downstream effects on platform and application layers

trend.trend_direction: Accelerating (open-source share accelerating upward, closed-source revenue dominance eroding but still commanding)
trend.year_over_year_change: Open-source token share: from ~30% (early 2025) to ~43% (late 2025), representing roughly 43% growth within a single year; Open-source model releases: 33.3% (2021) to 44.4% (2022) to 65.7% (2023); Enterprise Anthropic share: 12% (2023) to 24% (2024) to 40% (2025 year-end); OpenAI enterprise share: 50% (2023) to 34% (2024) to 27% (2025); Hugging Face model repository doubling time: from 1,000+ days to 335 days; Cost per token for open-source: continuing to decline with each major release (DeepSeek V3, Qwen, Kimi K2)
trend.compound_annual_growth_rate: Open-source AI model market CAGR: 15.1%-35% depending on analyst (market.us projects 15.1% CAGR 2025-2034; FutureDataStats projects 35% CAGR 2024-2032)
trend.forecast_value: Open-source AI model market: $54.7B by 2034 (conservative, market.us) to $100B by 2032 (aggressive, FutureDataStats); from base of ~$13.4-15B in 2024. On-premises LLM solutions projected to control over half the LLM market by 2026.
trend.velocity_indicator: adoption_doubling_time: Open-source token share roughly doubled from ~22% to ~43% in approximately 6 months (May-November 2025); Hugging Face model repository doubling time compressed from 1,000+ days to 335 days; Each major Chinese OSS model release (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi K2) captures sustained production usage within weeks

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: This is one of the most strategically important dynamics in the AI industry for startup founders. The data reveals a paradox that directly shapes business model decisions: open-source models now match closed models on performance (1.7% benchmark gap) and are 87% cheaper ($0.23 vs. $1.86/M tokens), yet closed models still capture 96% of revenue. This means: (1) The 'model as moat' thesis is collapsing — if you are building on a single closed API, your competitive position erodes with every open-source release; (2) The $24.8B annual 'unrealized value' from suboptimal model selection represents a massive arbitrage opportunity for startups that can intelligently route between open and closed models; (3) The enterprise market is fragmenting rapidly — OpenAI lost half its enterprise share in 2 years, meaning no vendor lock-in is permanent and switching costs are lower than assumed; (4) The hybrid approach is winning — enterprises use closed frontier models for cutting-edge tasks and open-source for cost-sensitive, specialized, or data-sovereign workloads; (5) For European startups specifically, open-source models enable GDPR-compliant on-premises deployment without sending data to US cloud providers, a critical advantage given EU data sovereignty requirements; (6) The DeepSeek moment showed that Chinese open-source models can disrupt market assumptions overnight, compressing the time founders have to establish market position.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Founders should architect AI products to be model-agnostic from day one — the model layer is commoditizing fast and vendor lock-in to any single provider is a strategic liability. Build switching capability and cost optimization into your inference stack. For cost-sensitive use cases, open-source models at $0.23/M tokens offer 8x savings. Consider a tiered approach: open-source for high-volume routine tasks, closed frontier models for complex reasoning. The Menlo Ventures data showing Anthropic's rise from 12% to 40% enterprise share in 2 years proves the market rewards quality and developer experience over incumbency — there is room for new entrants that nail the UX and tooling layer.

confidence.cross_reference: OpenRouter/a16z study (https://a16z.com/state-of-ai/) corroborated by Menlo Ventures enterprise data (https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-mid-year-llm-market-update/), Stanford HAI AI Index 2025 (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report), Red Hat Developer analysis (https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2026/01/07/state-open-source-ai-models-2025), CB Insights Foundation Model report (https://www.cbinsights.com/research/report/future-of-foundation-models-open-source-closed-source/), MIT Sloan open model analysis (https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ideas-made-to-matter/ai-open-models-have-benefits-so-why-arent-they-more-widely-used), California Management Review (https://cmr.berkeley.edu/2026/01/the-coming-disruption-how-open-source-ai-will-challenge-closed-model-giants/)
confidence.caveats: OpenRouter data reflects developer/API usage patterns, which skew toward technical users and may not fully represent enterprise procurement patterns or consumer-facing deployments (ChatGPT's 400M+ MAU are not captured). Menlo Ventures enterprise data may have sampling bias toward VC-backed companies. The 96% revenue share for closed models reflects pricing differentials as much as volume — open-source models cost 8x less per token, so even at equal usage volumes, closed models would dominate revenue metrics. 'Open-source' definitions vary — Meta's Llama has a commercial license with restrictions, and some models labeled 'open' are 'open-weight' without full training code/data disclosure. Hugging Face model count includes many fine-tuned variants and small models, inflating the count relative to truly novel model architectures. Market size forecasts for open-source AI vary dramatically (15.1% to 35% CAGR) depending on scope definitions.
confidence.measurement_reliability: analyst_estimate (Menlo Ventures enterprise share and spending), verified_financial_filing (OpenRouter token volumes are empirically measured platform data published alongside a16z), survey_self_reported (enterprise adoption surveys), projection_range (market size forecasts)
